title: A diagnostic routes support, never grades
statement: Use a diagnostic to route support under stated uncertainty, never as a grade or a mastery label.
detail: The course-quality checklist accepts a diagnostic only when its product type, sampling limits, uncertainty, slips, guesses, unassessed knowledge and routing behaviour are explicit and tested (`ti-courseplans-audit/docs/standards/student-course-quality/versions/2.0.0/GOLDEN-CHECKLIST.qmd`). The earlier version of the standard lists a diagnostic score that directly promotes, punishes or labels mastery, or hides its uncertainty, as a failure, and bounds the claim: a diagnostic may inform a later assessment but does not replace it (`ti-courseplans-audit/docs/standards/student-course-quality/versions/1.0.0/STANDARD.qmd`).
against: The grade 3 curriculum criteria doubt that a valid diagnostic of knowledge or comprehension gaps exists at all, and build breadth of knowledge instead (`ti-courseplans-audit/skills/g3-reading-red-team/references/dimensions/D7-knowledge-first-curriculum.md`); that bears on whether to build one, not on how to use one.

evidence.quote: Product type, sampling limits, uncertainty, slips, guesses, unassessed knowledge, and routing behavior are explicit and tested.
Failure signals: Diagnostic score directly promotes, punishes, or labels mastery; uncertainty hidden.
Claim boundary: A diagnostic may inform a later assessment but does not replace it.
